cutover_order: 1. Owner provides Shared Drive access to the company service account path (see the runbook owner action).
2. Create the 40_Content article folders for the three review docs through the governed folder operation, with fixed idempotency keys.
3. Copy the three review docs and their three source packages; compare names, MIME types and SHA-256 against this manifest.
4. Replay the copy; confirm zero new files.

5. Export the n8n Data Tables from Cloud (Raw_Media, Content_Cases, Photo_Content_Queue, Publication_Radar, Publication_Analysis, Website_Content, Website_Content_Sync, LinkedIn_Drafts) and import to self-hosted.
6. Rebuild one workflow at a time on self-hosted inactive, run a manual canary against a test folder, then switch the single trigger.
7. Pause the Cloud twin only after the self-hosted canary passes and the rollback step below is written down.
rollback: Originals are never touched, so rollback is: reactivate the Cloud twin (kept paused, not deleted) and delete only the corporate copies created under the recorded idempotency keys.

recurring_writer.suspect: MM-20 Publication Scout on its Monday trigger, then MM-21 Publication Fetcher: two causes that multiply. (1) Rediscovery resets status, drive_file_id and analysis_id, so the same publications are approved again every Monday. (2) MM-21 reads its candidates once per incoming item, so two approved items give four files.
recurring_writer.status: identified; reset mechanism strongly supported, not yet seen as a before and after change
evidence_for: The live MM-20 graph is active with a Monday 07:00 trigger, auto-approval capped at 2 per run, and a call to MM-21.
MM-21 executions on 2026-10-19, 10-12, 10-05 and 09-28 start at 02:00:34 UTC; the source files of those days were created seconds later, 4 per Monday, 2 publications twice each.
The workflow time zone is five hours ahead of UTC, which resolves the earlier Monday 07:00 against Monday 02:00 UTC question.

44 source files exist in the personal root while only 5 radar rows are in a processed state (3 analyzed, 2 approved_for_analysis) and 62 rows are candidate_for_fetch, every listed one with empty drive and analysis ids. That is consistent with publications fetched in past weeks having been reset, but the listing shows only the first 60 rows.
The live upsert maps status, drive_file_id and analysis_id from the new item, whose last two are empty, as the owner confirmed.
evidence_against_or_open: No row-level before and after of one publication exists, so the reset is inferred from state and graph, not observed.
Execution history before 2026-09-28 is not retained, so earlier weeks rest on file times only.
The 2026-10-05 and 2026-09-28 runs ended in error after the files were written; the failing step is unknown.
The fan-out cause of the doubled files is an inference.
